reasoning: Both attempts get the main parts right: an owning Charm module, cloned tables on each update, a useSignalState bridge, and a Charm-reading guard. A is a bit more robust. It validates names, skips updates that change nothing, doesn't block BlockPlacer.start, and keeps the project's require style. B mixes `@game` string requires and `const` into the code and starts the stock listener in line, ahead of BlockPlacer.start.

criteria.note: BlockStock.luau holds getStock/setStock privately, exposes getStock/getCount, and writes only in onStockChanged.
setStock updater does table.clone(stock), sets one entry, and returns the original when the count is unchanged.
The guard reads BlockStock.getCount(blockType) directly from Charm, but there's no shared computed for the selected count or can-place; the UI derives it again in BlockPicker.
Main.client creates `VideCharm.useSignalState(BlockStock.getStock)` inside app() and passes it down as a source; tiles select by name.
Count, background, text color and the 'n left' label are bound to the Stock/Selected sources; missing counts show blank and are not grayed.

criteria.note: The updater is pure; the only listener is the useSignalState one, which Vide cleans up; start yields outside Charm.

criteria.criterion: 7. Correct, in scope, typed, checks pass
criteria.note: Only the client files plus BlockStock change; names are validated against BlockTypes.ByName; task.spawn keeps BlockPlacer.start from waiting; all checks pass.
BlockStock.luau keeps the signal private, exposes getStock and :GetCount, and writes only from onStockChanged.
The updater clones the stock, sets one entry, and returns the new table.
The guard calls BlockStock:GetCount(name), which reads Charm directly, but the selected count is derived separately in the UI with no shared computed.
useSignalState(BlockStock.getStock) is created in app() and passed as a source to BlockPicker.
Tile color, count text and the SelectedCount label are reactive functions of the Stock/Selected sources; they're blank before the first update.

criteria.note: The updater is pure; StartAsync's WaitForChild is outside Charm; no stray effects.
